1d9b395ae6119b97b035eed0b0634607a7f0d9a3.summary: Malpedia family page for Crimson RAT, first discovered in 2017 and used against organizations around the world. The page says it is often distributed through phishing emails or by exploiting vulnerabilities in outdated security software. Once installed it can steal data, spy on users, take control of infected computers, lock them, and extort payments. The page lists many third-party reports, mostly by title, linking the malware to APT36 and Transparent Tribe activity against India. The page itself makes no attribution.
